articles.title: Meep, meep. ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ opens with $15.5 million, ‘Spider-Man’ stays No. 1 for fifth weekend
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Three years after Warner Bros. abruptly canned “Coyote vs. Acme,” the Looney Tunes feature film that was given a new lease on life by Ketchup Entertainment debuted with an estimated $15.5 million in ticket sales over the weekend.

articles.summary: A section of the southbound Highway 400 in Vaughan was closed overnight due to a serious collision. Emergency crews were called to the on-ramp at Major Mackenzie Drive just after 1:45 a.m. for a crash involving two vehicles. Two people were rescued and transported to a hospital with serious injuries. The southbound lanes of the […]

articles.title: Toronto cinema says it was forced to cancel screenings over decades-old, unofficial 'zone' system
articles.summary: A downtown Toronto cinema says it was forced to cancel screenings of a new movie after the film’s distributor unexpectedly withdrew access — citing a decades-old practice in Canada that limits which theatres can show movies first.

articles.title: Investors prosper and consumers pay as the Iran war exacts an uneven economic toll 6 months in
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — As the U.S. and Israel relentlessly bombed Iran in the opening days of war, the most dramatic predictions of the conflict’s toll were unsparing: surging oil prices, worldwide recession and economic catastrophe.

Toronto police were called to their Queens Quay West and Dan Leckie Way area just before 7:30 p.m. Saturday, where they located a man suffering from stab wounds. articles.title: Buck Martinez inducted into Blue Jays' new Hall of Excellence at Rogers Centre
articles.summary: John Albert (Buck) Martinez, a cancer survivor, catcher, manager and broadcaster for parts of five decades with the Toronto Blue Jays, was inducted into the club's new Hall of Excellence on Saturday.

articles.title: Sports club hosts charity match in Scarborough for those impacted by Nepal flooding
articles.summary: A Toronto sports club hosted a community charity match in Scarborough to support those impacted by catastrophic flash floods in Nepal, as rescue efforts in affected communities entered their fourth day on Saturday.

articles.title: Ontario premier unveils Lake Ontario sign in Hamilton as tensions with U.S. escalate
articles.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a Lake Ontario sign in Hamilton on Saturday, after U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order to change the name to "Lake America" amid deteriorating relations.

articles.title: Family alleges fare inspectors used excessive force on Black man with disabilities in Newmarket
articles.summary: A Newmarket mother is alleging her 21-year-old son with disabilities was the victim of excessive force and racial profiling at the hands of fare inspectors on York Region Transit. The Canadian Civil Liberties Association says the case highlights the need for greater oversight of law enforcement on public transit.

articles.title: Man in his 60s dead after two vehicles collide in Brampton, police say
articles.summary: A man in his 60s is dead following a two-vehicle collision in Brampton, Ont., Friday, police say.

articles.title: Andreescu, fellow Canadian Draxl lose in final round of U.S. Open qualifying
articles.summary: No Canadians will enter the singles draws at the U.S. Open through the qualifying tournament after Bianca Andreescu and Liam Draxl lost in final round action Friday in New York.

articles.title: Ontario's top court sides with lower court, rejects developer's challenge over Greenbelt land
articles.summary: The Ontario Court of Appeal has sided with a lower court in rejecting a developer's constitutional challenge of a 2023 law that returned 15 parcels of land to the Greenbelt.
